words.meaning: Splitting a large database into smaller pieces spread across servers.
words.everyday: Like splitting a huge phone book into A–M and N–Z so two people can search at once.
words.work: We moved to sharding when the database got too big.
words.gap: ___ lets the database handle more users.
words.plain: We split the database into parts on different servers.
words.model: We use sharding.

words.meaning: When copies of data may differ briefly but will match up soon.
words.everyday: Like news spreading round a village: not everyone hears at once, but soon everyone knows.
words.work: With eventual consistency, a new comment may take a second to appear.
words.gap: The system uses ___, so updates can take a moment to appear.
words.plain: Copies of the data match up after a short delay.
words.model: The system has eventual consistency.

words.meaning: Retrieval-augmented generation: an AI looks up relevant documents before answering.
words.everyday: Like a student allowed to check the textbook before answering an exam question.
words.work: We use RAG so the chatbot answers from our help centre.
words.gap: With ___, the assistant quotes our own policies.
words.plain: The AI looks things up in our documents before answering.
words.model: The AI uses RAG to answer from our documents.

words.meaning: An attack where hidden text tricks an AI into ignoring its instructions.
words.everyday: Like slipping a fake note into the post that says "the boss says give this person the keys".
words.work: A web page used prompt injection to make the bot leak data.
words.gap: Treat web content as data to guard against ___.
words.plain: Someone hid instructions in a document to trick the AI.
words.model: The document contained a prompt injection.

words.meaning: When a model learns its training data too closely and does badly on new data.
words.everyday: Like memorising last year's exam answers and failing when the questions change.
words.work: The model's accuracy dropped on real data because of overfitting.
words.gap: Great test scores but poor real results suggest ___.
words.plain: The model learned the examples too well and fails on new ones.
words.model: The model is overfitting.

words.meaning: A database that stores embeddings so you can find items with similar meaning.
words.everyday: Like a library shelved by topic, so similar books sit together.
words.work: We store document embeddings in a vector database.
words.gap: Search runs on a ___ of embeddings.
words.plain: We keep the meaning-based search data in a special database.
words.model: We use a vector database for search.

words.meaning: Shrinking an AI model by storing its numbers with less precision.
words.everyday: Like saving a photo at lower quality so it takes less space but still looks fine.
words.work: Quantisation lets the model run on a laptop.
words.gap: ___ made the model four times smaller.
words.plain: We made the model smaller by storing numbers less precisely.
words.model: We shrank the model with quantisation.

words.meaning: A pattern that stops calls to a failing service so the whole system doesn't crash.
words.everyday: Like the fuse box in your house that trips to stop a fault spreading.
words.work: The circuit breaker stopped the payment outage spreading.
words.gap: A ___ stops one failing service taking down the rest.
words.plain: We cut off calls to the broken service automatically so nothing else fails.
words.model: A circuit breaker cut off calls to the broken service.

words.meaning: Describing AI that can plan and take actions on its own to reach a goal.
words.everyday: Like a personal assistant who books the whole trip, not one who just suggests flights.
words.work: We're testing an agentic workflow that files expense claims.
words.gap: An ___ assistant can complete tasks, not just answer questions.
words.plain: The AI can plan and carry out tasks by itself.
words.model: The AI is agentic.
